Science

The GED Science test gives you a text, a table, a graph, or an experiment, and asks what you can conclude from it. This course teaches the science you need and, above all, how to read and reason with scientific information.

Topics 1 to 5 are ready. Their fifteen lessons, each with a practice page, are linked below. We are writing the other topics now, in English and in Spanish; this page shows the whole plan.

How it is organized

  • 24 lessons in 8 topics, about 4 hours of study each, from the method of science to a timed practice test.
  • Not by levels, but by area. Science is organized by the three content areas of the GED test: life science, physical science, and Earth and space science. The skills topics (1, 2, and 8) come before and after them.
  • The eight science practices of the GED (SP.1 to SP.8: reading science, designing investigations, reasoning from data, evaluating conclusions, and more) run through the whole course. Each lesson says which ones it works on.
  • Three reporting categories. The test reports your score in three parts: analyzing arguments, evidence, and texts (30%); applying scientific processes (40%); and reasoning with numbers and data (30%). Each lesson shows the category, the depth of knowledge (DOK), and the standards aligned with each practice, and ends with GED-style questions.
  • Where to start: Topics 1 and 2 first, because they teach the skills the other topics use. After that, the areas can be studied in any order. Math Level 2 (graphs, percents, mean and median) is a good base.

Topic 1 The scientific method and research design

  1. 2.1Scientific notation, units, and the TI-30XS calculator

Life science

About 40% of the test

Topic 3 Life science I: the cell, energy, and the human body

  1. 3.1Cell theory, organelles, and the cell membrane

Topic 4 Life science II: heredity, evolution, and ecosystems

  1. 4.1DNA, RNA, and gene expression

Labs and simulations

  • Interactive pages already used in the Spanish course will come into LearnGED, in both languages: building and reading graphs, a virtual lab to design experiments, statistics with experimental data, and arguments with evidence.
  • Simulations for physics and Earth science, such as a roller coaster (energy), a pendulum, plate tectonics and earthquakes, the solar system, and the water and carbon cycles.
  • The TI-30XS calculator and the formula sheet, as in Math, wherever a lesson uses numbers.
↑ Back to top

How each lesson works

  • Lesson and practice page. Each lesson has its own practice page with activities that make new exercises every time, linked by section.
  • Two tries. First wrong answer: a hint. Second: the solution, explained. Two-choice questions explain right away.
  • English and Spanish. Both versions are built from the same source, so they teach exactly the same thing.
  • GED and CCR standards at the end of each lesson, taken from the official GED Assessment Guide.
  • Accessible. Keyboard navigation, text descriptions for every figure, larger text and high contrast, and nothing to install.
  • Everything on LearnGED. No accounts, no outside sites: the readings, the tools, and the practice live here.
